title: Write Moon in Ashwini, Magha and Mula
body:
The Moon's nakshatra is the first thing most people look up, and right now the Moon in Ashwini, Magha and Mula (the nakshatras ruled by Ketu) has a reading composed by the program rather than written by a person.

**What to do**

1. Read [content/README.md](packages/interpretations/content/README.md) and [STYLE.md](packages/interpretations/content/STYLE.md). Moon in Rohini in `content/planet-in-nakshatra/moon.yaml` is a worked example.
2. Add entries keyed `ashwini`, `magha`, `mula` to `packages/interpretations/content/planet-in-nakshatra/moon.yaml`: a one-sentence `summary`, one to three paragraphs of `detail`, and short `strengths` and `challenges`.
3. Run `npm run content -w @vedic/interpretations` and `npm test -w @vedic/interpretations`. Update the snapshot if the Gandhi chart uses one of yours.
4. Add your name under `credit:` if you would like to be on the credits page.

One nakshatra per pull request is fine; say which you are taking in a comment so two people do not write the same one.

Your own words, please: no text from books, sites or other programs.

title: Write Jupiter in Punarvasu, Vishakha and Purva Bhadrapada
body:
These are the three nakshatras Jupiter rules, so Jupiter is "at home" in each, and they deserve better than the composed reading.

Create `packages/interpretations/content/planet-in-nakshatra/jupiter.yaml`, copying the two header lines from `moon.yaml`, and add entries keyed `punarvasu`, `vishakha` and `purva-bhadrapada`. Then run `npm run content -w @vedic/interpretations` and `npm test -w @vedic/interpretations`. See [content/README.md](packages/interpretations/content/README.md) and [STYLE.md](packages/interpretations/content/STYLE.md).

Your own words, please: no text from books, sites or other programs. Add your name under `credit:` to be on the credits page.

title: Verify the Pancha Mahapurusha yoga citations
body:
`packages/interpretations/content/yogas.yaml` cites Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa, Malavya and Sasa to Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, with Phaladeepika ch. 6 and Saravali as further sources, all marked `verified: false`.

If you own a printed translation (for example R. Santhanam's BPHS), check the chapter and verse, put it in `ref`, set `verified: true`, and fill in `edition` (translator, publisher, year) and `verifiedBy`. If our rule in `src/yogas.ts` disagrees with the text, say so in the pull request: that matters more than the citation.

Run `npm run content -w @vedic/interpretations` before committing; `COVERAGE.md` will show the new count.

title: Verify the lunar yoga citations in Brihat Jataka
body:
Sunapha, Anapha, Durudhara and Kemadruma are cited to Brihat Jataka ch. 13 (Chandra yogas), unverified, in `packages/interpretations/content/yogas.yaml`. Check them against a printed translation (B. Suryanarain Rao's or V. Subrahmanya Sastri's, for example), add verse numbers to `ref`, set `verified: true` and name the `edition`.

Also check our Kemadruma cancellation (any planet in a kendra from the Moon or the ascendant) against the text, and say in the pull request if the text is stricter or looser.

title: Verify the Nabhasa (Sankhya) yoga citations
body: The seven Sankhya yogas (Gola to Veena) are cited to Brihat Jataka ch. 12, unverified. Check them in a printed translation, add verse numbers, and set `verified: true` with the `edition`. If the text says when a Sankhya yoga is overridden by another Nabhasa yoga, note it in the `cancellation` field.

title: Verify the Phaladeepika ch. 6 yoga citations
body: About fifteen yogas in `packages/interpretations/content/yogas.yaml` cite Phaladeepika ch. 6 (Gaja Kesari, Chandra-Mangala, Lakshmi, the three Viparita and three Parivartana yogas, Vesi, Vasi, Ubhayachari, Adhi, Amala, Saraswati, Vasumati, Shakata), all unverified. Pick any of them, check the verse in a printed translation (G. S. Kapoor's or V. Subrahmanya Sastri's, for example), and set `verified: true` with the `edition`. Partial pull requests are welcome.

title: Find a classical source for Shubha and Papa Kartari
body: Shubha Kartari and Papa Kartari are cited as "Classical, widely cited, source to be confirmed". Find where the rule is stated (a text, chapter and verse), and update `citation` in `packages/interpretations/content/yogas.yaml`. If it is a later or modern formulation, say that instead, as we do for Guru-Chandala.

title: Simplify the ten hardest readings
body:
The bottom of [COVERAGE.md](packages/interpretations/content/COVERAGE.md) lists the ten English readings with the highest grade level. Rewrite one or more so they read more easily, without losing meaning: shorter sentences, shorter words, terms glossed in brackets. See the readability section of STYLE.md.

The composed nakshatra readings near the top are built from phrases in `src/i18n/phrases.ts`; a better phrase there improves 243 readings at once.

title: Gloss the Sanskrit terms in the yoga readings
body:
Some yoga readings use terms like kendra, trikona, dusthana and yogakaraka without explaining them (see `yoga:yogakaraka` and `yoga:dainya-parivartana`, the two densest). Add a short gloss in brackets the first time a term appears, for example "a kendra (one of the four angular houses)". The readability check in `test/readability.test.ts` stops counting a term once it is glossed this way.

The yoga text is in `packages/interpretations/src/yogas.ts`; the Hindi translations in `src/locales/hi/yogas.ts` do not need to change.

title: Add near-miss test charts for the Mahapurusha yogas
body: Every yoga has a chart that forms it in `packages/interpretations/test/fixtures/yoga-charts.json`. Add the opposite: for each of the five Mahapurusha yogas, a chart that *almost* forms it (the planet in its own sign but not in a kendra, or in a kendra but not dignified) and a test that it is **not** found. Put them in a new `test/fixtures/yoga-near-misses.json` and a short test beside `test/yoga-lint.test.ts`. `test/fixtures/chart.ts` explains the fixture format.

title: Start a Spanish reading pack with the Sun and Moon in each sign
body:
Spanish (`es`) is one of seven languages with no readings yet; everything falls back to English. A pack can start small. Create `packages/interpretations/src/locales/es/` modelled on `src/locales/hi/`, with only `planetInSign` for the Sun and Moon (24 readings), and register it in `src/i18n/context.ts` next to `hi`.

Translate the meaning, not word for word, and keep the tone of [STYLE.md](packages/interpretations/content/STYLE.md). COVERAGE.md will show your progress once `npm run content -w @vedic/interpretations` is run.

title: Do a clean build on your machine and report it
body:
We have never had someone other than the maintainer build the project from scratch. On a clean clone, run:

```bash
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm run content:check
npm run verify:ephemeris
npm test
npm run build:pages
npx playwright install chromium
npm run smoke
```

Comment here with your OS, Node version and the result (pass, or the first error). If something fails, a pull request that fixes the instructions is even better. You will be added to the credits either way.
